summary: Peter von Köppen was a historian and archaeologist. He studied at the National University of Kharkiv (~1809–1814) and the University of Tübingen (~1822–1823), later serving in the Ministry of State Property (~1837–1852).

Petr Sgall was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Charles University (~1945–1949), completing his doctoral studies under Vincenc Lesný, and later held a post at Charles University from ~1953 to 2008.

Petra Kieffer-Pülz is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Heinz Bechert. She held posts at the University of Göttingen (attested 1995), the Pali Text Society (~2012), and the Mainz Academy of Sciences and Literature (attested 2013, 2016).

Petra Maurer is a scholar of Tibetology and Indology who studied under Dunchu Sonam Dorje and Dieter Schuh. She held posts at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities, the University of Munich, IKGF Erlangen, and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

id: P:Petrus Abraham Samuel van Limburg Brouwer
summary: Petrus Abraham Samuel van Limburg Brouwer was an Indologist. He studied at the University of Groningen (1844–1850), earning a Dr.juris degree, and held a research post at the Nationaal Archief in 1865.

Phakchok Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Dzongsar Institute and under multiple traditional teachers, including Nyoshul Khenpo Rinpoche and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, and served as Vajra Master at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling.
Pham Thi Tuyet Tam is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the supervision of Somboon Vuddhikaro and Sanu Mahatthanadull (attested 2017).

Phanit Jetjiravat is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, advised by Phra Suthithammanuwat, Veerachart Nimanong, and Paetpong Worapongpichet.

Philip A. Kuhn was a sinologist and historian. He studied at Harvard, SOAS, the Defense Language Institute, and Georgetown. He held posts at the University of Chicago (1963–1978), Harvard University (1978), and the Fairbank Center for Chinese Studies (1980–1986).

Philip A. Mellor is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Manchester by 1989 and later served as Professor and Head of the School of Humanities at the University of Leeds (attested 2010).
Philip Anderson was an Indologist and historian. He studied at the University of Cambridge from ~1834 to 1838, earning a B.A., and later served as Vice-President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai.

Philip Boas Yampolsky was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Columbia University and under Yoshitaka Iriya. He held positions at Columbia University (1968–1996), the Numata Center (1991–1996), and Bukkyo Dendo Kyokai.

Philip C. Almond is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Adelaide (1975–1980) and served at the University of Queensland from 1982, becoming Emeritus Professor.

Philip Clart is a scholar of sinology and religious studies. He studied under Daniel L. Overmyer (~1991–1996) and became Professor of Chinese Culture and History at the University of Leipzig around 2008.

Philip Deslippe is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Connecticut (BA 1996–2000), the University of Iowa (MA 2008–2010), and UC Santa Barbara, where he was attested as a teaching associate in 2020.

Philip Kapleau was a Buddhist studies teacher who studied under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki, Soen Nakagawa, Sogaku Harada, and Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani. He founded the Rochester Zen Center and Chapin Mill Retreat Center (1996).

Philip L. Quinn was a philosopher and religious studies scholar who studied at Georgetown, Delaware, and Pittsburgh. He held posts at Brown University (~1970–1985), the University of Notre Dame (1985), and served as APA President (1994–1995).

Philip Lutgendorf is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Chicago (~1967–1987), joined the University of Iowa in 1985, and served as President of the American Institute of Indian Studies (2010–2018).

Philip Novak is a scholar in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Syracuse University and the University of Notre Dame, and took up a teaching post at Dominican University of California around 1980.

Philip Stanley Rawson was a historian, archaeologist, and Indologist. He studied at Winchester College, Oxford, the Courtauld Institute, and SOAS. He taught at the Royal College of Art and served as Dean at the University of London (~1981–1984).
